subject: Sizing follow-up: streaming token velocity & peak vs steady hypothesis
messages:
From: Priya Shah <pshah@cartly.com>

Subject: Post-call details: streaming UX / peak spikes / token averages

Thanks again for the call earlier. A quick post-call summary from our side and a few concrete numbers so you can sketch a sizing hypothesis.

Quick background: Cartly is planning a US-wide rollout of a conversational shopping assistant. The main flows are short interactive sessions (search/refine) plus an occasional long-form recommendation generation for curated bundles. We will use streaming to deliver token-by-token updates in the interactive path.

What we observed in our pilot telemetry (attached sample):
- Steady weekday baseline: ~20 qps overall (requests/sec) across the cluster, roughly 40k tokens/sec aggregated (avg ~350 tokens/request).
- Peak flash events (promo pushes): spikes observed up to ~420 qps for a 3–7 minute crest window (~peak tokens/sec ~147k).
- Concurrency: steady concurrent streams ~60, peak concurrent streams observed ~260 during crests.
- Session mix: ~75% short interactions (avg 1–3 messages, streaming enabled), ~25% long generation (non-streaming, avg 800 tokens).
- Latency targets we care about: first-token streaming latency ideally <120ms (p95), full response p95 <700ms for short flows. For long-form generation tolerable up to p95 2s.

Open asks for Redwood sizing:
1) Confirm approach for mapping these numbers to slot/burst sizing (how many dedicated GPUs or shared capacity we should expect for initial pilot at these load shapes).
2) Any perf optimizations you recommend (batching window, KV cache heuristics, quantization) to reduce unit costs without violating latency targets.
3) What telemetry format do you need from us to validate a sizing estimate (sample rate, fields)? I attached a small CSV export.

Thanks — happy to hop on a follow-up if that helps.

—Priya

Internal note before we produce a client-facing hypothesis. Priya sent concrete telemetry — see attached CSV. High-level thoughts:

- Peak-to-baseline ratio ~21x (420 / 20) during crests — that drives our autoscaling and burst requirements.
- Streaming first-byte SLO at 120ms p95 is aggressive but achievable with low-batch low-latency path; we should treat that separate from full-response SLO.
- We need to clarify whether the 420 qps peak is evenly distributed across regions or concentrated in a single region (affects routing/fallback). Priya: can you confirm all traffic is US-east for the promo?

Initial follow-ups for Jordan/Priyom:
1) Jordan — produce a quick sizing hypothesis (slots and expected qps capacity per slot) with two configs: a) latency-optimized (smaller batches, lower kv-cache hit requirements) and b) cost-optimized (larger batch tolerance, quantized model). Please include expected steady vs crest capacity per slot and recommended burst-window headroom.
2) Priyom — outline telemetry fields we need from the CSV to derive tokens/sec and concurrency time-series at 1s granularity. Also list any sample queries we should run in a lightweight benchmark to validate model-level latency.

I'll consolidate and send back to Priya with a proposed pilot sizing and concrete next steps. Target to have client note ready by tomorrow morning PT.

Quick sizing sketch (high level) — will turn into numbersheet for Marissa to send:

Assumptions from Priya's telemetry: avg tokens/req = 350 for interactive, avg tokens/req = 800 for long-form; steady qps = 20, peak qps crest = 420 for ~5 minutes.

Sizing hypothesis (per Redwood medium GPU slot — conservative perf profile):
- Steady-state: 1 slot handles ~2200 tokens/sec (streaming-friendly path with prefix caching). For avg 350 tokens/request => ~6 qps per slot steady. So for 20 qps steady => ~4 slots (headroom x1.5 => 6 slots).
- Peak crest: with dynamic batching and short burst optimization, a slot can sustain ~50 qps short-term (up to 2–5 minutes) => ~50 qps * 6 slots = 300 qps, still short of 420. To cover crest without throttling, recommend adding burst capacity (either reserve extra slots up to 9–10 for crest or configure cross-region fallback to spare capacity).
- Concurrency: observed 260 concurrent streams at peak; streaming slots should be configured to support ~30–40 concurrent streams each (varies by model); to cover 260 streams we'd want ~8–9 streaming-optimized slots during crest.
- Latency: first-token <120ms p95 requires low-batch path (batch size <= 8) and explicit KV-cache priming for common prefixes. Full-response p95 <700ms for short flows requires maintaining small aggregation windows.

Immediate recommendations for pilot:
- Pilot baseline: 6 medium slots reserved (predictable baseline + 50% headroom).
- Burst strategy: allow autoscale to add up to 4 additional burst slots (total 10) or pre-wire cross-region fallback for short crests.
- Model config: quantized medium model for cost path, with a faster fp16 dev path for latency-critical routes.
- Telemetry required: per-request tokens_in/tokens_out, request_start/request_end timestamps, stream-first-byte timestamp, region, session_id. 1s resolution preferred for crest detection.

I'll prepare the spreadsheet with the expected qps-to-slots mapping and include cost delta between reserved vs burst capacity.

—Jordan

Priya / Alex — thanks for the telemetry and the clear session mix. Attached is a concise sizing hypothesis (redwood-sizing-hypothesis-20280327.xlsx) that summarizes Jordan's sketch and our recommended pilot configuration. Executive summary below and concrete next steps.

Executive summary (pilot recommendation):
- Reserve 6 medium slots for steady baseline (covers 20 qps with 50% headroom for normal daily variance).
- Configure autoscale/burst to allow up to +4 slots for 5–7 minute crests (total 10) OR enable cross-region fallback to absorb extra load.
- Streaming tuning: batch size <= 8 for first-token path; enable KV prefix caching for common prompts; expect p95 first-byte ~100–140ms in latency-optimized path.
- Cost tradeoffs: using quantized medium model + dynamic batching lowers steady cost by ~25% vs always using latency-optimized fp16 model; details in attached sheet.

Action items & owners:
- Priya: confirm whether crest traffic is US-east only or multi-region (due Thu 2028-03-29).
- Priyom: send a 48-hour high-res telemetry extract (fields Jordan listed) so we can run a slot simulation (due Fri 2028-03-30).
- Jordan: finalize the qps-to-slot mapping and cost delta table and share the spreadsheet (ETA Fri morning PT).
- Marissa: schedule a 30-min sizing review with Cartly and infra on Mon 2028-04-02 (I will send invites once Priya confirms region).

If you prefer, Jordan and I can run a short benchmark (5–10 minutes) against a representative model with your sample inputs; that would validate the first-byte and full-response latencies before the pilot starts. Please reply with a list of 3–5 representative queries if you want that run.

Thanks — we’ll iterate after we get the telemetry extract.
